name: exact_compatible_procedure
description: Belt squeal on Chevrolet Cruze with exact GM TSB 19-NA-037 procedure retrieved. Should produce guide_available with cited steps.

causes.name: Accessory drive belt slipping or glazed

checks.question: Does squeal occur upon engine start and AC activation?
Are visible cracks or glazing present on belt ribs?

retrieved_sources.document_title: GM Bulletin 19-NA-037: Front End Accessory Drive Belt Squeal
retrieved_sources.text: 1. Turn ignition OFF and allow engine to cool completely. 2. Install a 3/8-inch breaker bar into the square drive on the belt tensioner. 3. Rotate tensioner clockwise to relieve belt tension and remove belt from alternator pulley. 4. Release tensioner gently and remove drive belt. 5. Route new GM drive belt around crank and AC compressor, rotate tensioner, and seat belt on alternator pulley.

fault.name: Accessory drive belt slipping or glazed
fault.evidence_summary: High-pitch squeal confirmed by physical check observing glazed ribs and supported by GM TSB 19-NA-037.

steps.action: Turn ignition OFF and ensure engine is completely cool before starting work.
steps.warning: Never touch belts or pulleys when the engine is warm or ignition is ON.

steps.action: Insert 3/8-inch breaker bar into tensioner square drive, rotate clockwise to release tension, and remove belt from alternator pulley.
steps.warning: Keep fingers away from pulley pinch zones while tensioner is under spring load.

steps.action: Remove old belt, route new drive belt around crankshaft and AC compressor, rotate tensioner, and slip over alternator pulley.

safety_warnings: Ensure the ignition key is removed so the engine cannot inadvertently turn over.
Ensure the new belt is properly centered in all pulley grooves before releasing tension.
limitations: If belt tensioner exhibits excessive flutter after replacement, the tensioner assembly may also require replacement.
mock_guide_output.recommendation: Start engine after replacement and inspect belt tracking. If noise persists, inspect alternator decoupler pulley.

Does squeal occur at idle?
checks.answer: No, only when steering wheel is turned all the way

retrieved_sources.document_title: Car Maintenance Tips: Power Steering Fluid
retrieved_sources.text: Locate the power steering reservoir near the front right corner of the engine bay. If the fluid level is below the Lower Level fill line, remove the cap and refill with approved power steering fluid up to Upper Level.

fault.name: Power steering pump strain or low fluid cavitation
fault.evidence_summary: User physical check confirms belt is in new condition, ruling out primary belt decay. Squeal occurring exclusively on full steering lock points to hydraulic pump strain or low fluid.

steps.action: With engine off, locate the power steering fluid reservoir in the engine bay and inspect the cold fluid level against the indicator marks.
steps.warning: Ensure engine is stopped before opening fluid reservoirs.

steps.action: If fluid is below the Lower Level mark, top up with manufacturer-approved fluid to the Upper Level line and re-seat cap securely.
steps.warning: Do not overfill beyond the maximum fill line.

safety_warnings: Avoid holding steering wheel at full lock for more than 5 seconds as this stresses the pump relief valve.
limitations: The underlying issue could involve internal pump cavitation or pressure valve wear if topping off fluid does not eliminate the noise.
mock_guide_output.recommendation: If squeal persists with correct fluid level, have the steering rack and pump pressure evaluated by a technician.
